It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. div.head: ECf 12a
div.ab: alia die qua primum coronatus est — ipsa habet octo dies —; in natali Domini VIII dies et VIII dies pasche et VIII pentecostes;
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 637 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

note.seg: repeated at 27; cf. Hn 10, 1, note h

also erste Woche jeden Regierungsjahres, die bekannt war, da die Königskanzlei nach letzterem datirte. Da Verf. primum hervorhebt, dachte er wohl noch den König dreimal jährlich, an den drei Hauptfesten, unter Krone gehend, was 1139 für ein halbes Menschenalter aufhörte

so the first week of each regnal year, which was known because the royal chancery dated by it. Since the author stresses primum, he was probably still thinking of the king wearing his crown three times a year, at the three chief feasts, which stopped in 1139 for half a generation
ausserdem herrscht an den drei Festen Gottesfrieden laut 2
besides, the peace of God prevails at the three feasts, according to 2
fehlt Hk; cor. est pr. Hr Ad Do
lacking in Hk; cor. est pr. Hr Ad Do
in n. D. VIII d. fehlt Hr
in n. D. VIII d. lacking in Hr
in pascha similiter et in pentecoste similiter Hk
in pascha similiter et in pentecoste similiter Hk
d. pa. VIII dies pent. VIII dies Ad Do

div.ab: another, on the day on which he was first crowned — this has eight days —; at the Nativity of the Lord eight days, and eight days of Easter, and eight of Pentecost;

note.seg: Ebd. Krönung 8. a. Die Klöster zu Westminster, Winchester, Gloucester beschenkt Heinrich I. jährlich zu einem der drei Hauptfeste, an dem er dort Krone tragen wird; Robinson Gilb. Crispin 141. Vgl. zu demselben Brauche in Deutschland und Frankreich Hatschek Engl. Verfassgschi. 68

Ibid. Krönung 8. a. Henry I makes annual gifts to the monasteries at Westminster, Winchester, Gloucester at whichever of the three chief feasts he will wear his crown there; Robinson Gilb. Crispin 141. On the same custom in Germany and France cf. Hatschek Engl. Verfassgschi. 68
